newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes scripless trade for commercial papers.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes scripless trade for commercial papers.

text.p: The Philippine Central Depository Inc (PCDI) is planning to register domestic commercial papers within the year to facilitate scripless trading in the secondary debt market, PCDI officials said on Thursday.
"There's a definite plan within the year that we can start (with) the CPs," PCDI debt operations manager Lee Garrido told reporters.
PCDI is currently registering equity stocks. As of today, 71 out of the 310 issues are already trading on a scripless system.
Garrido said negotiations have started with the different investment houses regarding the mechanics of the registration.
PCDI vice president for operation Jerome Arcangel said the scripless trading of commercial papers will help develop the growth of the corporate debt instruments.
"The better trading and settlement system will improve the corporate debt market," Arcangel said.
As of end-April, outstanding short-term commercial papers totalled 5.865 billion pesos, while long-term commercial papers amounted to 52.52 billion.
There are only 23 short-term commercial papers and 33 long-term commercial papers outstanding in the market.
Scripless trading of government securities is being handled by the Bureau of Treasury.
PCDI is owned by the different financial institutions including the Philippine Stock Exchange, the Bankers Association of the Philippines and the Investment Houses Association of the Philippines.
